name: Chamalal
catalog_quote: Слова могут оканчиваться как на гласный, так и на согласный. Ударение слабое динамическое, подвижное. Оно выполняет смыслоразличительную функцию. [Words may end in either a vowel or a consonant. Stress is weak, dynamic, mobile. It performs a meaning-distinguishing function.]

Слова могут оканчиваться как на гласный, так и на согласный. Ударение слабое динамическое, подвижное. Оно выполняет смыслоразличительную функцию. [Words may end in either a vowel or a consonant. Stress is weak, dynamic, mobile. It performs a meaning-distinguishing function.]

sources.citation: Borise, Lena. 2020. Word stress in the languages of the Caucasus. Preprint of chapter in M. Polinsky (ed.), The Oxford Handbook of Languages of the Caucasus (OUP 2021). lingbuzz/004203, 33 pp.
sources.quote: 'According to Magomedova (1981:103), stress in the Gakvari dialect of Chamalal, too, can be strong or weak. Stress often targets the initial syllable but can appear further to the right too; long vowels do not necessarily attract stress. Initial stress can be either strong and weak, while non-initial stress can only be strong. There are minimal pairs based on stress strength and placement: mú:na skin.INF, mù:na go.INF; χòχa bean-pod, χoχà straw (Magomedova 2004: 27).' ... 'strong stress tends to stay on the same syllable throughout the paradigm, while weak stress tends to be mobile ... Plural

sources.citation: Borise, Lena. 2018/2020. Tone and intonation in the languages of the Caucasus. Preprint of chapter in M. Polinsky (ed.), The Oxford Handbook of Languages of the Caucasus (OUP 2021). lingbuzz/004204, 30 pp.
sources.quote: 'Dialects of Chamalal have been analyzed as possessing various tonal properties, with some contradictory descriptions. Kibrik et al. (1978: 44) analyze Low Gakwari Chamalal as contrasting four tones (H, L, R, F) on the stressed syllable only, while Kibrik & Kodzasov (1990: 325) describe it as specifying each syllable for one of the four tones ... For Gigatli Chamalal, Kibrik & Kodzasov (1990: 324) postulate both a system of four tones ... and word stress. Stress targets a syllable with a R or F tone, if a word includes one. Otherwise, stress and tone are not correlated.'

sources.citation: Kibrik, A. E. & S. V. Kodzasov. 1990. Sopostavitel'noe izučenie dagestanskix jazykov. Imja. Fonetika. Moscow: MGU. (already on file from the chir1284 audit, not re-fetched sources)
sources.quote: Overview: 'Словесное ударение в дагестанских языках всегда подвижное и неавтоматическое'; Andic languages incl. Chamalal (N. Gakvari, Gigatli) analysed as syllable-tone systems (H, L, R, F), 'обычно отсутствует словесное ударение (исключение – гигатлинский диалект чамалинского)'. Gigatli §3: 'Ударение неавтоматическое, подвижное. Если в слове есть скользящий тон (R, F), то ударение, как правило, падает на него.' N. Gakvari §3: four syllable tones with many minimal pairs (has'/H слюна – has'/L жена; muna/HH шел – muna/RR свежевал), no fixed stress position stated.
